ref_extractions.title: EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original dataset paper that explicitly introduces and describes the OpenBMI dataset with three paradigms (MI, ERP, SSVEP). It defines concrete ML tasks with labels: binary MI classification (left vs right hand), ERP classification (target vs non-target), and SSVEP classification (multiple frequencies). The paper reports baseline decoding accuracies and BCI illiteracy rates for each paradigm.

ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Original dataset publication describing 54 subjects, 2 sessions, 62 EEG channels, with explicit task definitions and baseline performance metrics for all three paradigms

ref_extractions.title: Adaptive transfer learning for EEG motor imagery classification with deep Convolutional Neural Network
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses the OpenBMI dataset for motor imagery classification. feasibility_reason: Multiple relevant references confirm the OpenBMI dataset contains three well-defined classification paradigms (MI/ERP/SSVEP) with explicit task definitions, 2-class structures, and published baseline performance metrics across 54 subjects and 2 sessions. The original dataset publication (GigaScience, DOI 10.1093/gigascience/giz002) is corroborated by an independent transfer learning study that explicitly uses this dataset for motor imagery classification.

event_annotations.notes: No event IDs could be extracted from the OpenBMI dataset. The dataset contains .mat files with MATLAB struct 'EEG_MI_train' that includes event-related fields (y_dec, y_logic, y_class, class, t, ival, time_interval), but the read_mat tool could not extract subfield values - it only displayed the structure dtype and always showed the large 'x' EEG data array regardless of parameters attempted. The raw event IDs and their mappings to class names exist within the 'y_dec'/'y_class' numeric fields and 'class' string field, but these values are inaccessible with available tools. The dataset filename pattern 'sess{XX}_subj{YY}_EEG_MI.mat' indicates two sessions of motor imagery data, but no explicit event ID list was found in any readable file.
